Build prompt

Rebuild this interaction 1:1: Monopoly Go's age slider - on the "MY AGE IS..." consent card, dragging the slider scrubs the age value live (0 -> 99+), and the moment any value is chosen, the I AGREE button switches from disabled grey to bright green.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
A rounded card over a dimmed game background: Mr. Monopoly-and-dog illustration on top, "MY AGE IS..." headline, the age value in a small pill, a horizontal slider with 0 at left and 99+ at right, fine-print consent text, and a full-width I AGREE button at the bottom.

## Motion spec
Pattern: direct-manipulation slider with activation flip.
- Drag the slider thumb: the thumb tracks the finger 1:1 and the age pill updates every frame (integer 0..99, then "99+" at the cap), following the thumb with a tiny lag spring (translate, ~600/30, 80ms settle).
- The slider's filled track (blue) extends to the thumb as it moves.
- First value change: I AGREE flips from grey/disabled to green/enabled instantly (color snap, no transition) - the card is now submittable.
- Thumb press scales up 1.0 -> 1.15 while held; release scales back with a small bounce (spring ~400/20, 200ms).
- The value pill pops (scale 1 -> 1.2 -> 1, 150ms) when crossing each decade (10, 20, 30...).

## Calibration
- The pill's spring lag is subtle - readable while scrubbing, never trailing behind the finger's stop.
- Green activation happens on the first input only - no re-animating on later scrubs.

## Reduced motion
Thumb tracks without scale effects; pill updates without pops.

## Don't miss
- The value lives in a small pill above the slider, not on the thumb.
- 99+ is a distinct capped state - the pill text changes format there.
